subject: measEq.syntax error: Could not compute standard errors!

messages.author: 1bbbf684dcdb1170
messages.subject: measEq.syntax error: Could not compute standard errors!
parts:
Hello,

I am conducting CFA/measurement invariance and am assessing fit of four established models in the literature before conducting invariance testing of the best-fitting model.

When using the measEq.syntax function for the CFA portion of the analyses, I keep getting the following errors:


Here is one of the models:
EDEQ.3factor <- 'BodyDisL=~ NA*ede6 + ede10 + ede11 + ede23 + ede26 + ede27 + ede28 + ede12 + ede22 + ede24 + ede25
EatConL =~ NA*ede5 + ede7 + ede8 + ede9 + ede19 + ede20 + ede21 
ResL =~ NA*ede1 + ede2 + ede3 + ede4
BodyDisL ~~ EatConL + ResL
EatConL ~~ ResL
BodyDisL ~~ 1*BodyDisL
EatConL ~~ 1*EatConL
ResL ~~ 1*ResL'

I typically do not use a referent indicator when doing measurement invariance. But, for the configural model, I tried removing the NA*ede6 so that it would fix the first loading by default. The factors are highly correlated, so I specified that in the model, but I tried removing that portion of the syntax as well. So, I tried a model that was just this:

EDEQ.3factorRI <- 'BodyDisL=~ ede6 + ede10 + ede11 + ede23 + ede26 + ede27 + ede28 + ede12 + ede22 + ede24 + ede25
EatConL =~ ede5 + ede7 + ede8 + ede9 + ede19 + ede20 + ede21 
ResL =~ ede1 + ede2 + ede3 + ede4'

Both ways, I got the same errors about model identification.

However, when I don't use the measEq.syntax() function and instead use the cfa function, I don't get those errors. Any ideas why this might be happening? Should I not use measEq.syntax until I proceed to invariance testing? But won't I get this error when running the configural model?

For reference, here is my syntax:
OGmodel<-measEq.syntax(configural.model=EDEQ.original, ID.fac = "std.lv", parameterization = "theta",
                     ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016", group = "gender1", 
                     ordered = c("ede1", "ede2", "ede3", "ede4", "ede5", "ede6", "ede7", "ede8", "ede9", "ede10", "ede11", "ede12", "ede19", "ede20", "ede21", "ede22", "ede23", "ede24", "ede25", "ede26", "ede27", "ede28"))
model.OG<-as.character(OGmodel)
fit.OGmodel<-cfa(model.OG, data=tgednsmall, group="gender1", ordered=c("ede1", "ede2", "ede3", "ede4", "ede5", "ede6", "ede7", "ede8", "ede9", "ede10", "ede11", "ede12", "ede19", "ede20", "ede21", "ede22", "ede23", "ede24", "ede25", "ede26", "ede27", "ede28"))

Just using CFA:
fit.OGmodel2<-cfa(EDEQ.original, data=tgednsmall, std.lv=T, group="gender1", c("ede1", "ede2", "ede3", "ede4", "ede5", "ede6", "ede7", "ede8", "ede9", "ede10", "ede11", "ede12", "ede19", "ede20", "ede21", "ede22", "ede23", "ede24", "ede25", "ede26", "ede27", "ede28"))

I have just started using the measEq.syntax function because I like the option to use the Wu & Estabrook method, but recognize I might be doing the syntax incorrectly.

Thank you for any help!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: measEq.syntax error: Could not compute standard errors!
parts: Any ideas why this might be happening?
You generate syntax using the theta parameterization:

OGmodel<-measEq.syntax(configural.model=EDEQ.original, ID.fac = "std.lv", parameterization = "theta",
                     ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016", group = "gender1", 
                     ordered = c("ede1", "ede2", "ede3", "ede4", "ede5", "ede6", "ede7", "ede8", "ede9", "ede10", "ede11", "ede12", "ede19", "ede20", "ede21", "ede22", "ede23", "ede24", "ede25", "ede26", "ede27", "ede28"))
But you don't set that when you fit the model:

fit.OGmodel<-cfa(model.OG, data=tgednsmall, group="gender1", ordered=c("ede1", "ede2", "ede3", "ede4", "ede5", "ede6", "ede7", "ede8", "ede9", "ede10", "ede11", "ede12", "ede19", "ede20", "ede21", "ede22", "ede23", "ede24", "ede25", "ede26", "ede27", "ede28"))

So your syntax is specifying residual variances (fixed to 1 in the configural model) which should be simply implied by other model parameters under the default delta parameterization.  If you want to test strict invariance, then you need to use theta parameterization to generate the syntax AND to fit the model.  If not, then you could just use the default delta parameterization (statistically equivalent, but more numerically stable under certain conditions).

Also, make sure you label the argument ordered= for your vector of variable names, so lavaan knows what you are trying to tell it:

Just using CFA:
fit.OGmodel2<-cfa(EDEQ.original, data=tgednsmall, std.lv=T, group="gender1", c("ede1", "ede2", "ede3", "ede4", "ede5", "ede6", "ede7", "ede8", "ede9", "ede10", "ede11", "ede12", "ede19", "ede20", "ede21", "ede22", "ede23", "ede24", "ede25", "ede26", "ede27", "ede28"))
